triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The §122 temporary import surcharge was zeroed on the witness's exemplar-line flags (entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b) rather than on the source's actual exemptions (the 9903.03.03 exclusion list and §232-covered articles), suppressing the surcharge on China-301 list-1 and aluminum-membership lines of every origin.

triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a rename or as pure new coverage and could not: `entry_is_line_a`/`entry_is_line_b` were not renamed one-to-one but split across four distinct legal meanings in the same pre-fix file (§122 exemption at line 2571, China-301 list-1 membership at 2993, China-301 2024-action at 2994, §232-aluminum membership at 2743/2750), so the §122 exemption branch was gated on exemplar-line identity that traces to no source text. The pinned corpus confirms the actual source rule: Proclamation 11012 (FR 2026-03824) exempts only Annex I/II enumerated articles and articles "subject to additional import restrictions imposed pursuant to section 232", and states the surcharge "is in addition to any other duties" — nothing exempts §301-listed lines, which the pre-fix `entry_is_line_a` branch zeroed for every origin. The rule's own proof atoms for `versions[1].formula` already cited "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" and the 9903.82.02/.04 metals carve-out, so the module claimed that scope and the old condition did not implement it; the fix re-grounds the branch rather than adding unclaimed coverage. The bundled `section_232_steel_component_rate` addition is genuinely new coverage, but the §122/Brazil/forced-labor gate rewrites are corrections, and untraceable_branch (a condition with no basis in the cited source, re-grounded by the fix) is the right kind.
